chunks: And from him, from Fadala, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'It is not appropriate to enter into ihram before the time designated by the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), unless one fears missing the month in Umrah.'
And whoever vowed to enter ihram before the miqat, then it is obligatory upon him to enter ihram from the place from which he vowed; he narrated that.

key_terms.إِحْرَام: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.الْمِيقَات: The designated time or place for entering ihram

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on entering ihram before the designated miqat time?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between the obligatory miqat and voluntary vows, emphasizing that premature ihram is generally impermissible unless one fears missing the Hajj season. It highlights the juristic principle that a specific vow (nadhr) to enter ihram at a non-standard location creates a binding obligation from that specific spot, reflecting the flexibility within Shia fiqh for individual circumstances.
